template_metadata.purpose: This template aims to help you create a README for your data. Fill in only the sections that are relevant to your dataset; delete the rest.
guidelines: Anything inside brackets [ ] is an example and should be replaced with real answers or be deleted.
The symbol > signifies comments to the user, and should be deleted after the README is filled.
The symbols - - - signify separation of sections and do not need to be deleted.
The README file name starts with an underscore _ in order to make it appear first in the list of files, when sorted alphabetically.

This file is using markdown. By changing the blank lines, symbols and spaces you can break the format. If you wish to keep the file only as a text file this does not affect you. If you plan to use markdown, or transform the file to json or other format later, keep this in mind when editing.
After filling in the README you can delete the first page with instructions.

brief_description.comment: Write 2–3 sentences describing what the dataset contains and what it is used for.

research_context.comment: Write a brief description of the research project in which the data were produced. What were the goals? What questions was the research intended to answer?

related_publications.comment: List of publications (articles and data) where the data were used or presented, or if they are relevant to understanding the dataset.
placeholders: [(Annotation, e.g. Data retrieval) Citation of publication 1]
[(Annotation, e.g. Methodology instructions) Citation of publication 2]

directory_structure.comment: Describe the directory structure. If the structure is complex, you may describe it in text and/or visually using a directory tree, like the one below.

file_descriptions.comment: List the data files showing what each file contains. For large datasets, refer to an accompanying file description. If the content is evident from the file name, describe only the directory structure.

encoding.comment: Fill in according to the nature of the data, (e.g. for tabular data)

variable_descriptions.comment: List the variables of the data. Include the variable name, data type, unit (if relevant), a brief description, and examples or value ranges where applicable.

special_values.comment: Explain how special values are represented in the data, such as missing data, unknown values, infinity, etc. Specify which concrete values or codes are used for these purposes.

collection_creation_of_data.comment: Describe how the data were obtained: methods, tools, time period, collection location, etc.

original_data.comment: Describe the original data including DOI, if available

method_of_collection_production.comment: Describe the method of data collection/creation

processing.comment: If the data were produced by transforming other data, describe the original data and the transformation applied. Describe the data processing steps: cleaning, transformation, anonymisation, formatting etc.

method_of_data_processing.comment: Add the software names (with version) used for the data processing. You can also simply describe the processing workflow, if no software was used.

data_completeness.comment: Describe data quality, known limitations, missing values, etc. How was the quality tested? Did you perform an integrity check?

license_and_terms_of_use.comment: Include the license text or link where it can be found, any copyright notice and any specific conditions for use of the data, for example if individual files are licensed differently.

restrictions_and_recommendations.comment: State any additional restrictions or recommendations for use.

software_and_hardware_requirements.comment: Describe the software and tools required to work with the data.

proposed_citation.comment: You may also include a dataset citation of a specific style, or use the template below: OR Please provide the dataset citation metadata in .bib and/or .cff format and reference the corresponding file(s) in the README.
placeholders: [Creator (Publication Year): Title. Publisher. (Resource Type). PID. Version]
[Citation for this dataset, compatible with Zotero and similar managers, are provided in the `_citation.bib` and/or `_citation.cff` file.]

ethics_and_data_protection.comment: Fill in only if the data contain personal data or sensitive information. If the data contain no personal data, delete this section.

personal_and_sensitive_data_protection.comment: Describe how the protection of personal/sensitive data was ensured, if the data contains sensitive information.

ethical_approval.comment: If ethical approval was required, state:
ethical_approval.placeholder: [Approved by the ethics committee name, approval number: xxx, date: YYYYMMDD.]

informed_consent.comment: Provide information on whether and how informed consent was obtained from participants.

acknowledgements.comment: You may thank collaborators, research participants, funding providers, etc.
acknowledgements.text: This README was based on the template/examples authored by the [Collective of Data Stewards of the Czech Data Stewards Community](https://github.com/Czech-Data-Steward-Community/README_FILES/blob/main/Collective_datastewards.md) and is licensed under a [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
